text:
ellie: quick thought — for the benchmark launch posts can we try a slimline chart set? smaller, single-axis, focused on latency per 1k tokens vs $/1k tokens. want something snackable for social and hero image on the blog.

maria_g: love that. do you mean 2 charts side-by-side (latency and cost) or a single scatter with slices?

ellie: prefer a single 2-panel image: left = latency histogram (median + p95), right = unit-cost waterfall (batching, quant, infra). simple labels, no gridlines. keep annotations to one sentence each.

sanjay: +1. also suggest we add a tiny callout arrow on the latency chart showing "real-time burst" behavior for small seqs. helps the product message about predictable tail latency.

alex_t: agree. for data callouts we should use these numbers: median=65ms/token (fastpath), p95=220ms/token, cost baseline=$0.25/1k, after-opt=$0.09/1k. i'm pulling final runs now and will push csv to /figma/bench-exports.

jamie: tagging creative: @maria_g can you sketch the 2-panel in figma? keep brand colors soft, emphasize the delta not absolute numbers. link to previous comps: https://www.figma.com/file/bench-visuals

maria_g: on it. quick Q — for the waterfall, do we show batching and quantization as stacked bars or separate bars with arrows showing reduction?

ellie: stacked bars but with small % labels on top. add a dashed line representing hosted baseline so enterprise customers can see headroom.

marketing-bot: Deployment note — blog image size must be 1200x630 px for Twitter/OpenGraph. Reminder: keep text < 60 chars for OG overlay.

sanjay: also recommend a 1-liner for social that ties to product differentiation: "Same models, predictable inference economics — speed where you need it, savings where you don't." thoughts?

alex_t: that reads well. maybe tweak to: "Predictable inference economics: latency you can rely on, costs you can control." feels tighter.

ellie: use alex_t's line. next steps: alex_t uploads csv by EOD, maria_g posts figma draft by 10am tomorrow, i'll draft blog hero copy and pull CTAs. if anyone sees major number diffs once the run finishes call it out asap.

jamie: will prep alt headlines for A/B test in email and social.

ellie: perfect. thanks all :thumbsup:
